findings.message: Changing `time.proposal-hours-refresh` from an entity schedule to a tenant-wide one leaves the old per-entity rows in the database. `workflows.ensure_schedules` (packages/db/migrations/0017_workflows.sql:169) only inserts or updates rows, keyed on (tenant_id, name, legal_entity_id). It never deletes a row whose definition changed scope. So any database that already synced 104's version (dev, preview or a CI replica built from this branch) keeps one row per legal entity and also gains the new tenant row. The refresh then runs N+1 times a night. Entities with no time zone also keep their stale rows, which is the Settings hub miscount this change is meant to fix. Production is not affected because 104 has not merged, so this is minor. Fix: add a migration, or a cleanup step in the amendment, that deletes `workflows.schedule` rows where name = 'time.proposal-hours-refresh' and legal_entity_id is not null. Alternatively, make ensure_schedules prune rows whose scope no longer matches the definition.
findings.scenario: A tenant has 2 legal entities and its DB was synced with 104 (entity schedule). After this diff it syncs again → 3 schedule rows for time.proposal-hours-refresh. The refresh runs 3 times a night, and the Settings hub still counts the zone-less entity's row as waiting for a time zone.
